input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second § 12.4 imposes a non-compete on Customer that exceeds our walk-away threshold: it runs 24 months post-term, applies in any territory, and uses undefined scope ("any product or service that competes with Vendor"), also sweeping in acquisitions and internal development. It also contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We delete the clause to reach the preferred position, offering the narrowed fallback (single named product, term only, with carve-outs) if Vendor needs protection.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the 24-month, all-territory non-compete because we cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, and this clause directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. If Vendor needs protection for a specific offering, we could consider a restriction limited to one named competing product during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
